title: Stride-aware KV shadow coalescer for interleaved batching and GPU slab packing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: our current KV prefix reuse system successfully deduplicates identical prefix fragments across requests but struggles with interleaved batching patterns typical of multiplexed workloads. This causes suboptimal slab packing on GPU memory, higher fragmentation, and missed reuse opportunities when similar but non-identical token strides appear across concurrent requests.

Goal: implement a stride-aware 'KV shadow coalescer' that detects aligned header/segment fingerprint patterns across inflight requests, creates lightweight shadow entries that represent common stride variants, and enables compact GPU slab packing and prioritized prefetching without increasing tail latency beyond SLO. The feature should operate online with bounded CPU cost and be opt-in behind a runtime flag initially.
spec:
Overview:
1) Fingerprint model: compute a compact fingerprint for the first N token groups (configurable, default N=3) using a rolling Murmur3-based combiner and a normalized stride signature capturing token-length buckets (e.g., [<=32,33-64,65-128,>128]).
2) Shadow entries: when multiple fingerprints are similar within an edit-distance threshold over grouped strides, create a shadow entry that references a canonical fragment plus a delta descriptor rather than storing a full duplicate. Shadow entries include a similarity weight and residency credit used by eviction.
3) Stride-aware slab packing: modify the slab allocator to consider stride classes and co-locate shadow-linked fragments to contiguous GPU slabs to reduce internal fragmentation and improve coalesced memory reads during KV streaming.
4) Prefetch policy: extend request routing to emit lightweight prefetch hints when a match to a shadow's fingerprint crosses a configured confidence threshold. Prefetch is charged against a per-tenant prefetch budget to avoid noise amplification.
5) Async reconciliation: background job consolidates shadow entries, promoting high-utility shadows to canonical fragments and garbage-collecting low-utility ones.

Data structures and tuning knobs:
- Fingerprint length (N), stride bucketing config, similarity threshold (0-1 float), prefetch confidence (0-1), per-tenant prefetch budget (tokens/sec).
- Memory accounting: shadow descriptors must be under 1% of total KV memory by default.

Operational signals to emit:
- shadow_created, shadow_promoted, shadow_evicted, shadow_prefetch_hit_rate, slab_fragmentation_by_stride, avg_tail_latency_with_prefetch, prefetch_budget_utilization.

Backward compatibility: shadows are only consulted for read-paths; write-paths create canonical fragments as today. If a shadow is consulted but not present on GPU, fall back to current fetch path to avoid added latency.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests for fingerprint generation and similarity scoring (>= 90% deterministic coverage)
End-to-end benchmark shows >= 8% reduction in GPU KV slab fragmentation for mixed-text workloads (log-simulated multiplexing) at P50 latency within 3% of baseline
Prefetch hit rate > 60% for workloads with repeated stride variants without exceeding prefetch budget
No increase in 99th-percentile token generation latency beyond 5% on canary cluster
Feature gated behind runtime flag and documented in ops runbook
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (PoC): implement fingerprint generator and offline analyzer to identify common stride clusters from historical traces (owner: Luca)
Phase 2: runtime shadow descriptor and eviction credit integration with slab allocator (owner: AVS team)
Phase 3: prefetch hinting and tenant budget enforcement in router component (owner: routing-service)
Phase 4: canary rollout, observability dashboards, and ops runbook updates
Keep CPU work per request bounded; use sampled tracing (1% by default) for telemetry-heavy paths
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: over-aggressive prefetching increases upstream load and costs. Mitigation: enforce hard per-tenant budgets and adaptive backoff when prefetch hit-rate drops below threshold.

Risk: fingerprint collisions causing false positives and incorrect reuse. Mitigation: use conservative similarity threshold; fall back to canonical fetch if delta reconstitution fails checksum; add instrumentation for collision rate.

Risk: increased allocator complexity causes regressions. Mitigation: keep slab-packing heuristics orthogonal to main allocator and expose simple on/off flags; add thorough stress tests on simulated GPU memory workloads.

Risk: tenant isolation issues from shared shadow entries. Mitigation: shadow descriptors carry tenant scoping; do not share opaque payloads across tenants—only sharing of structural layout and canonical fragments when allowed by tenant policy.
Risk: maintenance burden of extra background reconciliation job. Mitigation: reuse existing checkpointing/compaction framework; schedule at low utilization windows and provide metrics for tuning.
testing_plan: Offline trace replay harness: extend existing trace-replay to synthesize interleaved multiplex workloads and measure slab fragmentation and reuse metrics
Microbenchmarks: fingerprint generator and similarity scoring latency/allocations
Canary cluster: enable on 1/10 of Dedicated pools for 48h and observe prefetch budget, tail latency, and error rates
Chaos test: simulate OOM and high eviction churn to validate reconciler correctness and safe fallbacks
rollout_plan: Feature landing behind flag in runtime-1.22 branch
Start with offline analyzer only (no runtime shadow creation) to validate clusters against historical logs
Enable runtime read-path shadow consultation on internal canary pools (non-customer)
Gradual customer canary: opt-in tenants via admin toggle, monitor signals for 72h
Wider Dedicated rollout after 2 successful customer canaries and sign-off from SRE
